notes: Residents: IMP block-level population layers (Densidad_Urbana_Mz2021 for Lima, Densidad_bruta_Callao for Callao). Jobs: INEI business census (CENEC) by block, published by IMP. Blocks with implausible job counts (far more jobs than establishments allow) were rebuilt from establishment counts, and 30% of jobs are treated as informal and spread in proportion to residents. Lima is scaled to 4.9 million jobs; Callao's jobs are estimated from its residents using Lima's jobs-per-resident ratio. Workers are residents scaled by the same ratio. The airport, port terminals, large malls and the main universities are added as their own demand points using public estimates. Everything is summed in 500 m cells. Commute flows come from a doubly constrained gravity model calibrated to an average straight-line commute of 8 km; no origin-destination data was used. Driving times assume road distance of 1.35 times straight-line distance at an assumed speed. Basemap, buildings and roads come from OpenStreetMap and Overture and are not used for demand. Data vintages follow what IMP publishes for each layer. The residents shown in the game are employed commuters only; they are derived from IMP's total-population counts by applying one uniform workers-per-resident ratio to every block, not from a measured count of employed residents. — Reviewer refinements (2026-11-05): scored against the deprecated lima record (kaicardenas0618, medium 0.50, backfill 2026-07-23) — same Lima + Callao frame, same two source types (economic-census jobs, census population by manzana). workplace_count re-ruled registered_self_declared, matching lima — the author's own cleaning found blocks with far more jobs than their establishments allow and rebuilt them from establishment counts (head-office booking, which the PE ruling prices as registered), and Callao (~1.1M people) carries no workplace data: its jobs are its residents × Lima's jobs-per-resident ratio. workplace_granularity re-ruled adm4 — block counts for Lima's formal jobs, a Lima-wide total for the 30% informal share and a province-level estimate for Callao; per §2 rule 3 the middle grain is recorded with bounds (adm5 / adm2). workplace_intensity re-priced fine_types_generic, not measured_per_unit — the informal share and all of Callao are placed by the resident distribution (cancun precedent: informality is priced once, on placement). Resident answers CONFIRMED as filed and equal to lima's: total_population (one uniform workers-per-resident ratio is a constant scaling) at adm5 × mesh_125_or_adm5 × measured_per_unit (IMP block counts, nothing spread below the block); summing into 500 m cells is point-placement detail, which §9 does not score. od_metric re-ruled synthetic_measured_marginals, not none — unlike lima's unconstrained gravity, the model is doubly constrained to measured residents and the CENEC job totals (gravity ruling; amba / merida rung); about 37% of the destination side copies the resident distribution (Callao plus the informal share), noted here for auditability. Alternatives on record: prior_informed_synthetic O/D (the strict reading of that 37%) 0.51, same medium tier; physical_measured jobs (the chennai / cdmx-core reading of an economic census as a real establishment enumeration) 0.600 (high), rejected given the rebuilt blocks and Callao; physical_inferred 0.57. PE floor (medium 0.50, lima and the other deprecated kaicardenas0618 maps) met. Revised high 0.67 -> medium 0.53.
